newsitem.title: KENYA: African leaders call for peace in eastern Zaire.
newsitem.headline: African leaders call for peace in eastern Zaire.

text.p: African leaders after a one-day summit called on warring parties in eastern Zaire to agree to a negotiated peaceful settlement, state-run Kenya radio said on Tuesday.

It quoted a statement by the eight leaders who met in Nairobi on Monday as urging warring parties to commit themselves to a negotiated settlement in eastern Zaire, where Rwandan-backed forces have rebelled for the past two months.
Kenyan officials said the leaders apparently did not meet on Tuesday, as was expected, and were now leaving for home. The Zaire government failed to send a representative to the Nairobi summit.

The radio said leaders noted with satisfaction the easing of the Rwandan refugee problem in eastern Zaire but were concerned security had deteriorated there since they last met on November 5, the radio said.
They called for international aid to resettle and integrate Rwandan refugees who returned to Rwanda from Zaire last month and urged those who remained in eastern Zaire and Tanzania to return home.
The radio gave no details. Kenyan Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka was due to hold a news conference later on Tuesday.
